title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries

reading.body:
Pizza Hut deployed an AI-powered delivery system called Dragontail that gave third-party delivery drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, allowing them to see order timing and strategically delay pickups to batch multiple deliveries together. This caused pizzas to arrive cold and late to customers, creating a failure in the core function of a delivery system: getting food to customers while it is still hot.

A major franchisee operating 111 locations in the Northeast claims the system caused over $100 million in damages and sharp performance declines after its 2024 rollout, including sales dropping from positive double-digit growth to negative single-digit growth in some markets. The franchisee alleges Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training or support before mandating the system's use. It is not established whether the system's design was flawed or whether inadequate deployment practices caused the damage.

reports.title: Pizza Hut's AI system caused 'cascading' problems and $100M in damages, franchisee alleges in new suit
Pizza Hut franchisee says AI caused $100M in damages
Frustrated franchisee sues Pizza Hut over crappy kitchen AI
A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries

summary:
A major Pizza Hut franchisee filed a lawsuit in Texas claiming the chain's new AI-powered delivery system, called Dragontail, caused massive operational problems and over $100 million in damages. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, says the system gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, allowing them to see order timing and wait up to 15 minutes to batch multiple deliveries together. This resulted in pizzas arriving cold and late to customers, causing significant customer dissatisfaction.

Before implementing Dragontail in 2024, Chaac maintained over 90 percent on-time delivery rates and double-digit sales growth. After the rollout, the franchisee experienced sharp performance declines, with New York City sales dropping from positive 10.19 percent growth to negative 9.78 percent year-over-year. Chaac alleges Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training or support and violated the franchise agreement by mandating use of the flawed system. Pizza Hut declined to comment beyond stating it would respond through legal channels. The lawsuit comes as Pizza Hut's parent company plans to close 250 U.S. locations this year amid broader business struggles.
